scope.title: My Interests — I Like Listening to Music

annualGrammarExplicit: past continuous versus past simple with when/while
programme.presentPerfect: textbook extension; not separately enumerated in annual list; no mandatory assessment decision

skills.target: Interpret music genres, instruments, people and activities in a supplied context
skills.route: Core automatic; choice, matching or bounded gaps; unique category criteria

skills.target: Distinguish deliberate listening from hearing and use taught voice/music expressions
skills.route: Core automatic vocabulary; meaning-based contexts, not a spelling-only contrast

skills.target: Use possessive determiners/pronouns with an unambiguous referent
skills.route: Supporting automatic practice; comparison language is prerequisite/reuse, not new comparison coverage

skills.target: Interpret taught place, movement and time prepositions
skills.route: Supporting automatic practice; text or reviewed purposeful diagrams

skills.target: Interpret and form present/past simple passive with explicit actor, receiver and time
skills.route: Core automatic; bounded fields, choice or ordering; no untaught perfect passive

skills.target: Distinguish adjective and adverb functions when the word form is unchanged
skills.route: Supporting automatic practice; compare with all Unit 1 S04/S07 history

skills.target: Use taught adjective–preposition combinations in a meaningful sentence
skills.route: Core automatic; reviewed alternatives and self-contained context

skills.target: Distinguish finished-past events from time-up-to-now/current-result meaning
skills.route: Textbook extension; present perfect is not separately enumerated in the annual Grade 7 list. Retain teaching and practice; mandatory Mastery inclusion needs an explicit Unit 2 scope decision.

skills.target: Distinguish background actions, completed events and simultaneous actions with when/while
skills.route: Core automatic; review all linguistically valid tense/conjunction alternatives

skills.target: Identify the main idea and purpose of a simple music information text
skills.route: Core automatic reading; immutable shared text set

skills.target: Retrieve and connect explicit musician/music details, distinguishing fact from evaluation
skills.route: Core automatic reading; evidence supplied, no celebrity knowledge prerequisite

skills.target: Identify the main message of simple music-topic speech
skills.route: Core automatic listening; exact reviewed recording required

skills.target: Retrieve relevant spoken details and distinguish stated positions/actions
skills.bookAnchor: p.39, ex.16/17; p.50, ex.29 as supporting practice
skills.route: Core automatic listening; music-topic sources needed for assessed T2.L1 coverage

skills.target: Write an informational description of a musical style and one example work, with reasons
skills.route: Teacher-reviewed extended writing; supplied fact card, no lyric copying or research requirement

skills.target: Respond respectfully in writing to another view about music and explain a reason
skills.route: Teacher-reviewed written interaction; can share one response with S14 but is not an independent second sample

activities.disposition: Instrument vocabulary. Keep meaningful visual recognition only with reviewed, labelled images/accessibility; text definitions may supply a separate vocabulary task.
Owner-directed replacement at the same position: One Song, Two Versions. C27B registered audio is linked to P63/P67/P68 under C31 with passing QA. Do-Re-Mi original and derivative remain excluded.
activities.replacementRecordingStatus: Registered and attached; C27A/C27B evidence reused. Independent human pace acceptance and fresh authenticated playback are not claimed.

activities.disposition: S02 hear/listen contrasts; supply tense and meaning context, including the different expression hear of.
S01 categories; replace ambiguous odd-one-out prompts with a stated category. Several listed music groups are valid peers.
S02 voice expressions; replace the alcohol example and give enough context for a defensible volume choice.
Preference vocabulary and optional written preparation; oral exchange in class, no right/wrong taste.
Optional self-reflection. Remove expertise/enthusiasm labels inferred from ticks; owning an instrument or reading music is not a proficiency score.
S01 music terms with unique keys. Repair overlapping sound/music and group-size options; avoid contested instrument/genre trivia.
S03 possessives with explicit referents. Do not require standalone possessive its; comparisons reuse prior teaching.
S04 prepositions; specify each relation and correct broad assertions such as nobody working during holidays.
Classroom survey/interview; optionally provide fictional responses for writing preparation without collecting classmates' data.
Optional survey-report writing from supplied data. Retain its place; not a substitute for the programme's style-and-work essay.
Optional picture narrative in the original panel order. Review coercive physical handling in the cartoon; keep it a narrative, not endorsed teaching behaviour or a core writing substitute.
Preference description and S14 preparation; reasons may support any genre.
Oral interview in class; supplied written comments may prepare S15. No live peer messaging required.
Track 5 shared listening. Test attributed speaker claims; do not teach its broad learning/stress claims as established causal facts.
Track 6 optional ability/listening support. Contextualize gendered dialogue; no pronunciation or repetition score.
Corrected world-musician information and reading; keep six profiles' order. Speaking follow-up in class; replace photo/name guessing with supplied evidence.
Corrected Armenian-musician information and reading; preserve the six-profile order and cultural topic. Complete the essay/response preparation here.
S05 simple passive; use explicit singular/plural and time cues.
S05 bounded gaps; repair ambiguous times and unsupported historical/political examples. No factual knowledge is required to infer grammar.
S06 adjective/adverb function; bold the intended word and compare with Unit 1 before counting novelty.
S07 adjective–preposition combinations; remove nationality stereotypes and unnecessary health assertions.
Rewrite instructions for mixed active/passive where required. Retain the paper-history topic with verified/cautiously framed information; no forced passive for an active subject.
Instrument/auction context for S05. Remove unverified record-price claims and perfect-passive dependence; supply explicit simple-tense time anchors.
S08 tense meaning; replace signal-word-as-command rules. Multiple-selection source items must be adapted to supported choice/categorisation contracts.
S08 contextual tense practice, with S09 cases kept in their later teaching sequence; correct incomplete or factual-trivia contexts.
S08 form/meaning recognition; declare category reuse, not an unsupported checkbox response type.
Track 7 supporting listening. C31 automated reconciliation confirms the room-cleaning inconsistency; P66/P72 avoid that detail and their keys are supported. Preserve the limitation and source family.
S04 meaningful spatial/movement relations. Nine picture panels and ten terms do not imply one-to-one matching; one staircase panel illustrates two directions. Specify cardinality or split prompts.
Optional phonetic-reading/recitation in class; no new publisher audio was identified here and no pronunciation assessment is planned.
S05 house-history practice; repeated verbs permitted as printed, bounded alternatives/context required. Keep this topic at its source position.
S09 finished versus in-progress past; remove cases where duration alone cannot determine a unique aspect.
S09 when/while; accept both when valid or rebuild the context. No universal short-action/long-action shortcut.
